instrument.state: Act on the reported 19 late starts among 74 bookings over six weeks and on competing explanations for why calendar availability did not translate into timely starts. Treat delayed returns, unfinished cleaning, inaccurate availability updates and delayed collection as hypotheses, not established causes. Assume records can be linked to equipment and bookings; verify this first. Distinguish scheduled start, physical return, cleaning completion, readiness for collection, collection and actual work start. Establish what the reported 'late start' measures and use the existing lateness rule, or agree one before comparison if none exists.
instrument.operation: During days 1–4, assemble booking-level timelines from the calendar and separate return, cleaning and collection logs. Review all 19 reported late cases and use the remaining bookings to check whether suspected problems also occur without lateness. Preserve missing entries and uncertain matches explicitly. For each material claim, record who observed what, when it was recorded, whether the source had direct access, and whether it copied another record. Seek independently grounded checks through existing crew and depot accounts or contemporaneous records where available; ask about specific events before presenting a proposed explanation. During days 5–8, prospectively check disputed handoff points within existing staffing, using separate firsthand observations where feasible. Reconcile conflicting timestamps, definitions and equipment identities without forcing agreement. By days 9–10, compare candidate changes against the corroborated failure patterns, their frequency and delay burden, operational feasibility and possible effects on other crews. Conditional candidates include a turnaround allowance for verified return-to-ready delays, a readiness confirmation before calendar release for verified status errors, or a collection handoff rule for verified collection failures. Select one narrowly scoped, reversible trial by the two-week deadline; do not combine changes whose effects could not be distinguished.
instrument.signal: Look for independent agreement or disagreement about the same equipment, booking and handoff. For example, a return entry and a separately recorded firsthand observation could support that equipment arrived after the next scheduled start; a cleaning entry and an independent readiness check could support that cleaning remained incomplete at that time. Calendar availability alone does not establish physical readiness. Record contradictions, unsupported intervals and missing coverage alongside supported sequences. Count supported patterns across bookings and note whether similar patterns occur among timely bookings. For the selected trial, prospectively observe late-start frequency and delay duration, readiness and collection times, completed or displaced bookings, and any added workload or unmet cleaning requirements.
instrument.inference: Convergence among credible sources with independent access increases support for the specific corroborated timing or status feature. Repeated supported sequences can justify prioritizing a corresponding change for trial, especially when their timing plausibly explains the delay and comparison bookings strengthen that explanation. Favor the feasible change addressing the largest credible, avoidable delay burden without purchasing equipment or adding staff. Contradictions lower confidence and direct follow-up toward the disputed handoff. If no explanation has adequate independent support by the deadline, select a limited readiness-confirmation trial primarily to resolve uncertainty, explicitly leaving its delay-reduction benefit unestablished. Compare trial outcomes with comparable baseline bookings, accounting for equipment, crew and demand differences; improvement supports continued testing but does not alone establish causation.
instrument.limit: Separate logs are not necessarily independent: they may share an author, copied timestamps, clock errors or assumptions. Retrospective accounts may share a narrative, and missingness may be concentrated in busy or delayed periods. Absence of an entry does not prove that an event failed to occur. Corroborated timing does not by itself establish the cause of lateness, and readiness, collection and work start are different events. Stop treating a disputed feature as established when source dependence, poor access or unresolved contradictions undermine it; retain competing explanations. Before trial launch, specify its duration, comparable bookings, success criterion and acceptable workload and access effects. Stop or revise the trial if it compromises required cleaning, safe use or essential crew access, or requires extra staffing. If too few comparable bookings occur, extend observation within existing resources rather than claim success or failure from inadequate evidence.
